arguments.content:
# Coupled pilot

Run the pilot using `scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py`.

## Case Selection

You can select specific cases to run using the `--case` flag multiple times.

Example:
```
python3 scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py --binary ./bin --repo ./repo --out ./out --provider openai --model gpt-4 --case alpha --case gamma
```

- Repeated `--case` flags select each named case once, preserving the original suite order.
- Duplicate case IDs in the flags are ignored; each case runs only once.
- If no `--case` flags are provided, all cases run by default.
- Unknown case IDs cause an immediate error before any output or execution.

This behavior ensures precise control over which cases run, while preserving the integrity and order of the original test suite.


- Duplicate case IDs in the flags are ignored; each case runs only once.
- If no `--case` flags are provided, all cases run by default.
- Unknown case IDs cause an immediate error before any output or execution.
- The default behavior without `--case` is to run all cases without filtering.

This behavior ensures precise control over which cases run, while preserving the integrity and order of the original test suite.

arguments.content:
# Coupled pilot

Run the pilot using `scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py`.

## Case selection

By default, all cases in the suite run in their original order.

To run a subset, use `--case` one or more times. Repeated flags are deduplicated and the original suite order is preserved. Unknown IDs cause an immediate error and no output or execution occur.

Example:
```bash
python3 scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py --case alpha --case gamma
```

This runs only the `alpha` and `gamma` cases, in that order, skipping `beta`.

Behavior summary:
- `--case alpha --case gamma` selects `alpha` then `gamma` (original order).
- `--case gamma --case alpha` selects `alpha` then `gamma` (original order).
- `--case unknown` fails immediately with an error and no output or execution.
- Omitting `--case` runs all cases in original order.
- The no-overwrite guard is preserved: existing receipts prevent re-execution.
